HM-04.c01: A **placarded vehicle** must show HazMat warning placards because of what it carries.
**Division 1.1, 1.2, 1.3** are the explosives divisions with mass explosion (1.1), projection (1.2) and mass fire (1.3) hazards.
A **safe haven** is a place approved, usually by local authorities, for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives.
**Shipper** sends the HazMat, **carrier** transports it, and the **consignee** receives it.
A **route plan** is a written plan of your roads, required for Division 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 explosives.
HM-04.c02: With Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 explosives, **never park within 5 feet** of the traveled part of the road.
Don't park within **300 feet** of a bridge, tunnel, building, place where people gather or open fire, except short stops such as **fueling**.
The vehicle must be **watched at all times**; someone other than you may watch it only on the **shipper's, carrier's or consignee's** property.
You may leave it **unattended** only in a **safe haven**, because an explosion near people or structures multiplies the harm.
HM-04.c03: Other placarded vehicles may park within **5 feet** of the road only if work requires it, briefly, and watched on a public road or shoulder.
Never uncouple and leave a HazMat trailer on a public street, and don't park within **300 feet** of an open fire.
The attendant must be in the vehicle **awake, not in the sleeper**, or within **100 feet** with a clear view, and know the hazards and how to move it.
Use **reflective triangles or red electric lights**, never flares, near Class 3 or Division 2.1 tanks (**loaded or empty**) or Division 1.1–1.3 explosives.
HM-04.c04: Finding out about **permits and special routes** before starting is **your job as the driver**; ask your dispatcher or check with state agencies.
When placarded, avoid crowds, tunnels, narrow streets and alleys even if inconvenient, and never drive near **open fires** unless you can pass without stopping.
Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 explosives need a **written route plan** that the **carrier** usually prepares and you carry and follow.
For placarded **radioactive materials**, the carrier must pick the **safest route** and show the driver the plan.
HM-04.c05: [CA] Carrying **any amount** of Division 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 or 1.6 explosives for hire means using **CHP** special routes, stopping places and inspection locations.
[CA] The same CHP routes apply to **more than 1,000 pounds** of these explosives in private carriage, and to bulk inhalation-hazard materials.
[CA] Use state or interstate highways with the least transit time; **operating convenience** is no excuse to leave a designated route.
[CA] Never leave a loaded vehicle unattended or parked **overnight** in a residence district.
[CA] You may leave the route for fuel, repairs, rest or food only at facilities within **1/2 mile** of the exit or entry point.
HM-04.c06: No smoking within **25 feet** of a placarded Class 3 or Division 2.1 cargo tank, or any vehicle with Class 1, 3, 4.1, 4.2 or 5.
Refuel with the **engine off**, and someone must always be **at the nozzle** controlling the flow.
The power unit of a placarded vehicle needs a fire extinguisher with a UL rating of **10 B:C or more**.
Check every tire at the **start of each trip** and **each time you park**, using a **tire pressure gauge**, the only accepted way.
Remove an **overheated tire**, place it a safe distance away, and fix the cause before driving.
HM-04.c07: Behind the wheel, keep HazMat papers within reach **with your seat belt on** or in the **driver's door pouch**, tabbed or on top.
Out of the vehicle, leave the papers in the **driver's door pouch** or **on the driver's seat** so responders can find them.
With Division 1.1–1.3 explosives, carry shipping papers, written emergency instructions, a written route plan and **FMCSR Part 397**.
Chlorine cargo tank drivers need an **approved gas mask** and a leak kit for **dome cover plate fittings**.
Placarded vehicles, any chlorine, and HazMat cargo tanks **loaded or empty** must stop **15 to 50 feet** before the nearest rail.
HM-04.c08: The **ERG** is DOT's guide for firefighters, police and industry workers, indexed by **proper shipping name and HazMat ID number**.
At an accident, keep people away, **limit the spread** only if safe, tell responders the danger, and give them the **shipping papers**.
Check your partner, **keep the papers with you**, keep people **far away and upwind**, warn others, call for help, and follow employer instructions.
HM-04.c09: Don't fight **HazMat fires** without training and equipment; you may use the extinguisher to keep a minor truck fire from reaching cargo.
Feel trailer doors first; if **hot**, don't open them, because air can make a cargo fire **flare up**.
Identify a leak from **shipping papers, labels or package location**; never touch it or **smell** it, since toxic gases can kill without odor.
Never drive on with HazMat leaking: **park it, secure the area, stay there**, and send someone for help with written details.
**Never repack** leaking containers; the **carrier pays** for cleanup, and the cost is enormous.
HM-04.c10: Class 1: **remove all explosives before separating** wrecked vehicles and place them **at least 200 feet** from vehicles and occupied buildings.
Class 2: **notify the shipper** if compressed gas is in any accident; Class 3: haul a leaking cargo tank only as far as a safe place.
Class 4: don't open **smoldering packages** of flammable solids; Class 6: many poisons are also flammable, so no smoking, flame or welding.
Class 7: after a radioactive leak, don't use the vehicle until it is cleaned and checked with a **survey meter**.
Class 8: **wash** vehicle parts that touched corrosive liquid thoroughly with water.
HM-04.c11: Call the **National Response Center** (**1-800-424-8802**) if a HazMat incident kills someone or hospitalizes an injured person.
Also call for property damage **more than $50,000**, public evacuation **more than 1 hour**, or a major artery closed **1 hour or more**.
Marine pollutant releases of **more than 119 gallons** (liquid) or **882 pounds** (solid) must also be reported.
Carriers send detailed written reports **within 30 days** to **CHEMTREC** (1-800-424-9300), which gives crews technical HazMat facts.
[CA] A HazMat spill on a California highway must be reported **immediately** to the CHP or police with traffic jurisdiction.
